## Answer length -- how to reply to the user
Default to a short answer plus an invitation to go deeper. Long, complete answers are the exception.

- Lead with the answer. First sentence states the conclusion or what was done. No preamble, no restating the question.
- Budget: under 150 words of prose, at most 5 one-line bullets. Code, diffs and tables do not count, but cite `file.py:42` rather than pasting code the user can open.
- Report results, not process. After tool work say what changed and whether it worked; narrate steps only on failure.
- Offer depth, do not deliver it unasked. Close with one line `Drill down: (a) ... (b) ... (c) ...` (max 3 real items), or omit it.
- Cut: option surveys you will not pursue, caveats that change no decision, recaps, closing summaries.

Full length is correct for: written deliverables (manuscripts, reports, files on disk), an explicit request for detail, and anything the user must know before an irreversible action.

## Writing style -- apply to ALL research text editing and drafting
Full guide: `C:\Users\rich\OneDrive - Danmarks Tekniske Universitet\JR\AI_auto\literature\Reference_Papers\STYLE_GUIDE.md`
Target register: Einstein (1905), Akerlof (1970), Kahneman & Tversky (1979), Ioannidis (2005).

**Do:** economy (cut every word that adds no force); concrete before abstract; active voice + first person plural (We show, We define); transitions with logical force (This implies, It follows that); one logical load per sentence; consistent terminology -- no synonym rotation.

**Cut immediately:** filler openers (It is worth noting that, It is important to note that); hedging (may potentially, could possibly, one might argue); meta-commentary (In this section we show that, We now turn to); AI-isms (delve into, showcase, leverage, robust, nuanced, paradigm, facilitate); inflation (highly significant, very important); wordiness (in order to -> to; due to the fact that -> because; utilize -> use); filler transitions (Furthermore, Additionally, Moreover).

## Session 2026-09-13
**Agent:** Claude Opus 5
**Goal:** Recalibrate the research writing style guide against the author's own published papers instead of the classic reference set alone, and record the choices so later edits cannot silently reverse them. Then apply the new rules to a live manuscript as the first test.
**Files touched:**
- `literature/Reference_Papers/STYLE_GUIDE.md` -- rewritten, +194/-87. New calibration target stated in the intro (the author's own voice with the AI tells removed; where the classics and the own papers conflict, the own papers win), five own papers listed as the primary reference, "Explain, do not compress" promoted to the first core principle above the old economy rule, permitted house vocabulary / limited / banned lists rebuilt from the corpus, substitution table, "Natural academic writing (anti-LLM pass)" section, and a new "Decision record (grilling session, 2026-09-13)" table holding 26 numbered picks.
- `literature/Reference_Papers/` -- five of the author's own papers added as the calibration corpus: Paulsen & Rich (2023, TR-B), Hipolito, Vandet & Rich (2022, Applied Energy), Borysov, Rich & Pereira (2019, TR-C), Rich (2020, Econometrics and Statistics), Rich (2024, Transportation).
- `literature/Reference_Papers/_own_samples.txt`, `_own_fulltext.txt` -- text extracts from those PDFs, used for the calibration and removed again once the guide was written.
- `~\.claude\CLAUDE.md` -- "Research writing style" section rewritten to match the guide: scope, sentence and paragraph shape, register and voice, the permitted connectives, structure, banned vocabulary and phrases, the replacement rule, mechanics, and the final pass. Saved 22:18.
- `~\.claude\skills\style-edit\SKILL.md` -- touched at 22:19, immediately before the run. No diff is available, the `scripts/_claude_backup` mirror is gitignored and carries the same timestamp as the live file.
**Outcome:** The guide is now calibrated on the author's own five papers rather than on Einstein, Akerlof, Kahneman & Tversky, Ioannidis and Dantzig, which are demoted to a secondary reference for register and the concrete-example habit. The decision record fixes the contested calls in writing: Furthermore is un-banned, "In this paper, we" and the roadmap paragraph are allowed, Firstly/Secondly/Thirdly is the enumeration form, colon lists become separate sentences, consequence openers must name their subject, the Latinate verbs (circumvent, render, entail, accommodate, employ, exhibit) stay, paragraphs run 6 to 10 sentences, and the length rule is structural rather than a word count. The replacement rule is the operative addition: a rewrite may not introduce a non-technical word that is absent from the author's own papers, which is what stops a banned-word fix from flattening the register. The guide was then exercised on `Pub_SAA_PMIP_MC` (see that project's log, session 2026-09-13): 71 edits over 61 paragraphs in 24 sections, and the run surfaced no rule that needed changing. Neither session was logged before the window closed, so both entries are written retrospectively on 2026-09-14.

## helpi command reference
Run: `helpi N AI_auto [-Force]`  (omit project where marked --)

| N  | Command                        | Project? | When to use |
|----|---------------------------------|----------|-------------|
| 1  | Create new project              | Yes      | Once per paper |
| 2  | Pull ALL projects from Overleaf | --       | Start of day |
| 3  | Pull ONE project from Overleaf  | Yes      | Before opening a project |
| 4  | Push local edits to Overleaf    | Yes      | After editing manuscript locally |
| 5  | Compile + open VS Code + PDF    | Yes      | Start of working session |
| 6  | Compile LaTeX + open PDF only   | Yes      | Quick recompile |
| 7  | Log + handover + open browser   | Yes      | End of session / checkpoint |
| 8  | Snapshot Overleaf (git tag)     | Yes      | Before major revision or submission |
| 9  | Rollback last N code commits    | Yes      | Undo bad code changes (PERMANENT) |
| 10 | Build submission package        | Yes      | Submitting a paper |
| 11 | Reviewer scaffold (.txt->LaTeX) | Yes      | After receiving reviewer comments |
| 12 | Reviewer draft loop             | Yes      | After annotating scaffold in Overleaf |
| 13 | Project status dashboard        | --       | Anytime |
| 14 | Open project network graph      | --       | Anytime |
| 15 | Open infrastructure guide       | --       | Anytime |
| 16 | Generate docs (HTML/PDF)        | --       | After editing infrastructure.html |
| 17 | Claude Code cheatsheet          | --       | Anytime |
| 18 | Toggle Claude model-check       | --       | Anytime |
| 19 | Generate Beamer slides          | Yes      | Before a presentation |
| 20 | Restore on replacement machine  | --       | Machine setup |
| 21 | First-time setup for new user   | --       | Machine setup |
| 22 | Compress AI log                 | Yes      | Auto-run by /close; manual on demand |
| 23 | Push code/ to GitHub            | Yes      | After code changes |
| 24 | Technical one-pager from paper  | Yes      | Anytime |

